name: Raids Are Infinite
teaser: TL;DR: Ever wished to just roam the map forever? Now you can!
description:
Overview

All playable raid locations have their time limits set to 99999 minutes on server startup. No more getting MIA because the raid timer ran out — take as long as you need.

Since v1.1.0 the mod also ships a client plugin that keeps the in-raid clock honest: raids start at your real system time and run 1:1 with it, the raid timer shows a wall clock instead of a countdown, and in Fika co-op every player’s sky matches the host’s.

How It Works

Server

The mod hooks into the database after it’s loaded and overrides EscapeTimeLimit, EscapeTimeLimitCoop, and EscapeTimeLimitPVE for every location that has a non-zero time limit. Locations with a value of 0 (unused maps) or 99999 (Hideout) are left untouched.

Since the override happens at runtime in memory, the database files on disk stay pristine — no integrity check issues.

Client

Raising the server-side limit alone isn’t enough — the client runs its own end-of-raid checks and its own clock, so the plugin covers four things the server can’t reach:

  • MIA is disarmed at the source. Rather than clearing the session timer (which breaks extraction, since Fika reads it unguarded), the plugin extends it to the year 2200. Every timer reader keeps working normally while the “time is up” comparison stays false for ~174 years, closing all three MIA paths at once.
  • Raids start at your real system time, running 1:1 with the clock instead of T*****‘s 7× acceleration. In Fika the host’s choice is published before the raid is created, so every client seeds from the same value.
  • The raid timer shows a clock, not a countdown. It renders the raid clock, so it matches the sky and is identical on every machine — not your local system time. Extraction and transit countdowns are left alone and still count down.
  • Client lighting is bound to the host’s clock. Fika syncs the raid clock but not the sky’s separate clock reference, so a client could stand in darkness inside a daytime raid. The plugin repoints the sky at the synced clock so it tracks it permanently.

The raid-setup screen also shows real system time instead of the accelerated backend clock.

Patched Locations

Location Stock Limit Co-op Patched
Customs 40 25 99999

Interchange 40 30 99999
Labs 35 30 99999

Reserve 40 30 99999

Streets 50 30 99999

Ground Zero (High) 35 30 99999
Labyrinth 40 30 99999
Arena 60000 60000 99999

Untouched: Hideout (already 99999), and the unused Private Sector, Suburbs, Terminal and Town (all 0).

Configuration

The infinite raid time itself is not configurable — that’s the whole point of the mod. The client plugin exposes a few display options in BepInEx/config:

Setting Default Effect
ShowClockInRaid true Show the current time on the raid timer instead of a countdown. Also forces the panel visible, which normally only appears in the last 10 minutes.
EnableLogging false Verbose trace output to the BepInEx log. Only needed when diagnosing.
LogIntervalSeconds 5 Throttle for repeated per-frame log lines.

Compatibility

  • SPT 4.1.x
  • Fika — supported but not required. The co-op time sync detects Fika at load and skips cleanly in singleplayer.

Installation

Standard drag and drop installation. The archive contains both SPT_Runtime/ (server mod) and BepInEx/ (client plugin) — extract into your SPT root so both land in place.

In Fika co-op, every player needs the client plugin, not just the host. The MIA checks run on each machine independently, so a player without it can still be pulled out as MIA while everyone else carries on.

Known Issues

In Fika co-op, a client’s raid clock can sit a fixed offset behind the host’s (roughly the time the client spent loading in). It’s constant, not drifting, and has no gameplay effect.
